Strategy Just Bought Bitcoin for the 4th Straight Week. So Why Aren't Crypto Investors Bullish on MSTR Stock?

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Strategy (MSTR +3.29%) has now bought Bitcoin (BTC -0.57%) four weeks in a row, with the most recent purchase disclosed on Nov.
  • The share price tells a different story.
  • According to recent reports, although Strategy has consistently purchased Bitcoin in November, it's not buying much, especially compared to past acquisitions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lyle Daly – Nov 27, 2026 at 8:43AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Strategy ›.

Strategy (MSTR +3.29%) has now bought Bitcoin (BTC -0.57%) four weeks in a row, with the most recent purchase disclosed on Nov. 23. Considering that Strategy is the largest Bitcoin treasury firm, you might think investors would be happy about this buying streak.

The share price tells a different story. Shares of Strategy reached a 52-week low of about $70 on Nov. 25, before rebounding to close at $80. Even after that recovery, Strategy stock is still down 39% since the start of the month. The Bitcoin acquisition approach has worked in the past, but this time, it feels more like a token gesture.

According to recent reports, although Strategy has consistently purchased Bitcoin in November, it's not buying much, especially compared to past acquisitions. Over the past four weeks, it has bought 2,789 BTC, and the last two purchases were the smallest: 485 reported on Nov. 16 and 457 on Nov. 23.

Those acquisitions account for just 0.3% of Strategy's total Bitcoin holdings, comprising 851,305 BTC. It's buying significantly less than it did earlier this year. For comparison, it bought 56,235 BTC in April and 25,404 BTC in May.

In a recent development, strategy operates a Bitcoin flywheel model, using equity, debt, and preferred securities to raise funds for Bitcoin purchases. Its stock previously traded at a premium to Bitcoin, which facilitated this approach. For much of 2024, Strategy's market valuation relative to the Bitcoin it held, or market-to-net-asset-value (mNAV) ratio, ranged from 2 times to 3 times. It could take advantage of that premium by issuing fresh shares and using the funds to buy Bitcoin.

According to recent reports, the company's mNAV has compressed to 0.94 times. Below 1, every share Strategy problems to buy Bitcoin dilutes shareholders.

In addition, most of the funds Strategy has raised from recent share sales haven't gone toward Bitcoin. They've moved toward buying back Stretch (STRC +1.08%), a preferred stock aimed at investors seeking passive income. Stretch is designed to trade near a $100 par value and had slipped into the mid-$90s. Leaving it there would threaten Strategy's ability to issue more preferred shares to fund future Bitcoin buys, so the organization is supporting the share price with buybacks.

From Nov. 16 to Nov. 22, Strategy sold 1,925,676 common shares, raising $176.7 million in net proceeds. It directed $147.0 million (83.2%) of those proceeds toward buying back Stretch shares -- alongside another $64.8 million from its cash reserves, for a total preferred buyback of $211.8 million -- while putting just $29.6 million (16.8%) toward Bitcoin. The priority has switched from acquiring as much Bitcoin as possible to defending the preferred stock.

NASDAQ · As of 10:44 AM ET 11/27/26.

Strategy is in a difficult position. MSCI revealed that it will remove Strategy from its global indexes, including the MSCI USA index, at the close on Nov. 30. JPMorgan Chase projects that the exit will lead to $2.8 billion in forced selling. Strategy is also underwater on its Bitcoin holdings, with an average cost of $75,446 per Bitcoin, nearly 25% more than it trades at now.

If you're bullish on Bitcoin, owning it directly or through Bitcoin ETFs is the safer option. Strategy served as a leveraged bet on Bitcoin in the past. Now, it needs to keep paying dividends on its preferred stock no matter how Bitcoin performs, and there's no telling if Strategy will be able to trade at a premium to Bitcoin again.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 27, 2026 at 8:54AM EST.
  • 10 stocks we like better than Oms Energy Technologies ›.
  • On its first half of fiscal year 2027 earnings call, held on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 27, 2026 at 8:54AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Oms Energy Technologies ›.

On its first half of fiscal year 2027 earnings call, held on Nov. 25, 2026, OMS Energy (OMSE +2.50%) unveiled that it no longer expects full-year revenue to exceed fiscal 2026 levels as customer delivery schedules slow. Oilfield equipment demand remains tied to customer project timing, but the company holds a record cash balance that shields operations during extended procurement cycles. Three things management said stand out.

Customer decision cycles extended in the Middle East, delaying call-off orders, which are delivery requests under existing framework agreements. Slower order placement in Saudi Arabia pushed first-half revenue down to $66.7 million from $82.8 million a year prior, forcing management to lower top-line expectations.

In a recent development, the tech giant ended September with $172.3 million in cash and zero bank borrowings, representing about $4.06 per share. That financial buffer allows the manufacturer to navigate market slowdowns and evaluate potential acquisitions without taking on debt.

Management aligned purchasing with active orders, cutting inventory to $7.7 million from $17.2 million six months earlier. That inventory discipline, combined with growth in higher-margin repair and engineering services, lifted gross profit margin to 31.4% from 28.2%.

Sources indicate that order approval cycles are slowing across key international markets, but management is executing on its backlog of $40.9 million in confirmed orders expected within 12 months. The manufacturer maintains long-standing relationships with national oil companies while expanding service capabilities in Southeast Asia, positioning it to capture demand when customer activity resumes.

With zero bank borrowings and substantial liquidity, the tech giant focuses on capital allocation discipline and organic capacity investment. Management is watching regional procurement timing while seeking strategic growth opportunities across Asia Pacific and the Middle East.

    Fire Sale: Here's Why Now May Be the Perfect Time to Buy Nvidia Stock

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (707 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that there are multiple reasons why Nvidia (NVDA -0.90%) is a great stock to buy right now, but investors must understand the risks, too.
    • Sources indicate that at the end of the day, I think Nvidia's stock is still trading at fire-sale prices.
    • According to recent reports, the Nvidia turmoil has been notable lately.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keithen Drury – Nov 27, 2026 at 9:18AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    It has been revealed that there are multiple reasons why Nvidia (NVDA -0.90%) is a great stock to buy right now, but investors must understand the risks, too. Fortunately, one of those risks just went away with Jensen Huang returning to the CEO position.

    Sources indicate that at the end of the day, I think Nvidia's stock is still trading at fire-sale prices. I think now is the perfect time to swoop in and scoop up shares, as a deal this good won't last forever.

    According to recent reports, the Nvidia turmoil has been notable lately. It all started with co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang resigning from his position after admitting being unfaithful to his wife. But then the board reinstated him a few days later. But he's not out of hot water yet, as he must appear before Congress to testify on Nvidia's chip shipments. A woman he’s alleged to have had an affair with is rumored to be a Chinese spy.

    NASDAQ · As of 10:43 AM ET 11/27/26.

    Another issue with Nvidia right now is concerns about how accurate its financials are regarding chip sales to China. The U.S. has banned the export of some types of chips. What was legally allowed to be sent directly to China was $2.4 billion for Nvidia in Q3, and it is no longer shipping these products to China.

    But what makes investors worried is how many chips were being sold to companies in other countries that were illegally diverting them to China. There are a handful of government entities that are probing Nvidia for these allegations, which could bring about fines. This comes with a risk of Nvidia potentially losing sales to some of these companies, which could affect Nvidia's total revenue.

    According to recent reports, however, I’m not worried. If there were a massive and obvious part of Nvidia's business that was being sold internationally that didn't add up to what domestic companies were spending on AI, this would have raised red flags long ago.

    While I think there may have been some (maybe a percent or two) of sales that ended up in places that they weren't supposed to be, the majority of Nvidia's revenue base is fine, and the companies behind that revenue base look like they are going to spend more next year.

    After the catastrophic sell-off, Nvidia's stock now trades for about 14 times earnings as I write this. For reference, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +1.23%) trades for about 20 times trailing earnings.

    So, even without any growth baked into the stock, Nvidia is trading at a discount to the broader stock market.

    In a recent development, when you factor in next year's estimated growth, this gets even more mismatched. During its Q3 conference call, then-interim CEO Colette Kress raised next year's revenue growth guidance from 70% to 75%. The reason is obvious: The AI hyperscalers are spending more and more on AI. This isn't going to change, and Nvidia's products practically sell themselves.

    When you factor in next year's potential growth, the stock trades for an unbelievable 9.3 times next year's earnings estimates.

    NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

    Those price tags are reserved for companies where failure is imminent or that have single-digit revenue growth. Nvidia is neither, and I think this fire sale could be one of the greatest opportunities to invest in Nvidia since the start of the AI arms race in 2023. While there will be some scary headlines that appear about Nvidia over the next few months, I think it will emerge OK, making now a perfect time to load up on shares, hold onto them for a few years, and massively profit.

    Tech Report: Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1116 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
    • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
    • The much more widely held B shares closed at fresh highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

    Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

    The much more widely held B shares closed at fresh highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

    The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

    Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

    Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

    After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

    They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

    Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

    We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the firm's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

    It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

    As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

    On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

    Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

    If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

    The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the firm as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

    The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

    According to recent reports, barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks new CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

    In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to quickly disclose any sales.

    Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

    That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

    Recent findings suggest that the case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

    Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

    Recent findings suggest that in the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

    All those numbers exclude the company's buybacks of its own stock.

    In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway states it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

    Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

    It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

    In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

    Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most notable ideas.

    It has been revealed that WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

    You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

    Two of the — well, all of the vital ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

    One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

    And the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

    And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that claims it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

    Berkshire market capitalization: $1,259,897,054,755.

    Berkshire Cash as of Sept 30: $377.4 billion (Up 3.3% from June 30).

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares in Q3 2026.

Two stocks do not a portfolio make, but I believe this is a strong starting point for many investors.

    It has been revealed that we asked our analysts what’s driving their investing this year. Their answers are worth borrowing as you initiative for 2027.

    Sources indicate that I will soon turn 54, and while I still feel like a kid, the fact is I’m not getting any younger. While I still love finding and investing in those great growth stories, I’m also slowly moving into more of a “protect your wealth” mindset.

    Recent findings suggest that retirement isn’t even a word in my lexicon today; I love what I do and where I get to do it and will keep on doing it as long as the Fool will have me. But last year I set out to really focus on dividend exposure in my portfolio and 2027 is going to be another year where that remains a top priority. Rest assured I’ll be checking in on our Dividend Investor service quite frequently.

    I recently read a book called Sport’s Perfect Storm: An Industry Now Totally Adrift, by Roger Mitchell.

    This line caught my attention: “In everything, the past is always prologue.”.

    After several years dedicated almost exclusively to reading investment books, this year, I’ve concentrated my leisure reading primarily on business history, and simply history. Learning about the past will give me a better perspective when investing for the future. Plus, this newly introduced focus feels particularly timely given that this year marks the 250th anniversary of American independence.

    As the late Charlie Munger once remarked: “There is no better teacher than history in determining the future. There are answers worth billions of dollars in a $30 history book.

    I want to think through and take bigger, bolder investment decisions that will play out decades from now. I want to find the compounding decade busters! By doing the research and building the conviction, you can build the investment positions.

    In a recent development, however, then it takes discipline and patience to see those investments play out over the next few decades. It’s often so counterintuitive: you get super excited about something newly introduced (the dopamine hit) and then you have to wait … and wait … and wait (the sugar crash). Rome wasn’t built in a day, and neither was a truly Rule Breaking portfolio.

    Recent findings suggest that I turned 57 this year, which puts me within a decade of retirement. I also know that many workers are forced to retire sooner than expected. So it’s probably time for me to start reducing my risk by beginning to build a bond tent that will get me through the “retirement danger zone”: a time when a bear market could delay my plans or force me to sell investments when they’re down.

    Sources indicate that however, like many Motley Fool members, I much prefer investing in stocks, and see investing in cash and bonds as the equivalent of being forced to eat broccoli because it’s good for me. (I don’t like broccoli.) So I will spend this year finding the balance between being prudent and pushing the envelope.

    According to recent reports, someone will ask if you’ve ever gotten one wrong. Here, three analysts share the moment a stock gave them pause, and what they did next.

    Sources indicate that alphabet (GOOG +0.02%) is one of my oldest, high-conviction portfolio positions. However, there was a period where I (along with many other investors) was concerned that its core search infrastructure might be unprepared for an AI universe disrupted by ChatGPT, despite it having invented much of the transformer architecture behind modern AI.

    Recent findings suggest that today, Alphabet is positioning Google Cloud as a primary growth engine, with an impressive backlog largely driven by enterprise AI adoption, it’s designing its own AI silicon through its custom TPUs, and is successfully integrating AI tools that keep people within the Google ecosystem. While capex is substantial, it has the margins and cash position to maintain its trajectory without compromising a profitable growth story, and that’s a value proposition I continue to believe in.

    It has been revealed that I first researched Pinterest (PINS +6.32%) in 2019 and was instantly enamored with the potential. The user base was smaller than other platforms, yet growing fast. And it was undermonetized. I called it an “exponential growth opportunity” because it could stack user growth on top of monetization growth.

    It has been revealed that my investment thesis for Pinterest appears broken, which is why I finally sold last year. Plenty of smart Fools think I’m wrong, and that may ultimately prove to be the case. But its most recent quarter showed only 17% growth in ad impressions and a 4% drop in pricing. In my view, the platform is getting oversaturated with ads, and many advertisers still aren’t willing to pay a premium price after all these years.

    According to recent reports, I’ve long admired Oracle’s (ORCL +2.00%) specialized “RDMA” server technology that’s so well suited to handle AI workloads, and in the several quarters since I finally bought in, my shares have appreciated handsomely. It’s loaded with debt however, and I’ve looked to super extended debt maturities as a mitigating factor. However, a slate of 2025 and 2026 borrowings for data center build-outs bent my buy thesis — I felt the “ick” after some back-of-the-napkin math!

    It has been revealed that my thesis didn’t break, due to explicit capital allocation and free cash flow assurances the company shared at its 2026 Investor Day in late October. But I continue to train a critical eye on capital expenditures, free cash flow, and the balance sheet strength of the cloud-based tech titans I own.

    None of the analysts claim to know where the market is headed next — and that’s the point. They focus on businesses, not stocks, and make investment decisions accordingly.

    Recent findings suggest that you can bring that exact discipline and mindset to Thanksgiving. If someone asks what the market will do in 2027, it’s fine to skip the guesswork. Shift the question instead and ask, which businesses they’d want to own for the next decade, and why.

    That’s a conversation worth having over dessert. And for anyone just getting started, remind them that every great portfolio starts with a single first step.

    From all of us at The Motley Fool, Happy Thanksgiving. Fool on!

    If a younger relative asked you over pie for one rule or piece of advice to build real wealth over the next decade, what would you tell them?

    Berkshire Hathaway’s CEO, Greg Abel, Just Bought $9.6 Billion Worth of 1 of Buffett’s Favorite Stocks

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (858 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 27, 2026 at 9:45AM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.
    • Sources indicate that greg Abel became the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.04%) (BRKB +0.32%) at the beginning of this year after the conglomerate's longtime leader and legendary investor, Warren Buffett, stepped down.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 27, 2026 at 9:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

    Sources indicate that greg Abel became the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.04%) (BRKB +0.32%) at the beginning of this year after the conglomerate's longtime leader and legendary investor, Warren Buffett, stepped down. Abel has had a busy first year in charge of the organization, and many of his moves have been reminiscent of those his mentor would have made.

    In a recent development, that's not surprising. Abel was quick to reassure investors that Berkshire Hathaway's values and culture wouldn't change under his leadership, and we have seen plenty of evidence that he meant those words. For instance, during the third quarter, Berkshire Hathaway spent $9.6 billion buying one of Buffett's favorite stocks. Here's what investors need to know.

    In a recent development, greg Abel. Image source: Getty Images.

    Industry observers note that when people try to guess Buffett's favorite stock, Apple (AAPL +1.00%) is usually near the top of the list. That makes sense. Apple has been in Berkshire Hathaway's public equity portfolio since 2016; it has been the conglomerate's largest holding for years, and Buffett once mentioned it is probably the best business in the world.

    Sources indicate that buffett has also praised Apple's now-former CEO, Tim Cook, on multiple occasions. However, there is one stock Berkshire Hathaway has spent even more on over the past decade or so: its own stock.

    Recent findings suggest that yes, Buffett loves Apple. But under his leadership, Berkshire Hathaway spent far more on share buybacks than it did on buying Apple shares over the past 10 years. That policy has continued under Greg Abel, who oversaw the conglomerate's $9.6 billion in buybacks during the third quarter.

    NYSE · As of 10:45 AM ET 11/27/26.

    Like most corporate strategies, share buybacks aren't inherently good or bad. A lot depends on the details. But they do tend to signal management's confidence in the company's outlook. Massive buybacks are a sign that a corporation's top executives believe shares are undervalued relative to the business's growth potential.

    If that's really the case, then buybacks, by lowering the total number of outstanding shares, increase intrinsic value per share. Of course, the opposite is true if shares are actually overvalued. Where does Berkshire Hathaway stand right now? We can always trust Buffett and Abel's judgment. After all, Buffett crushed broader equities in his six-decade tenure as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway.

    Industry observers note that few people are more capable than he is at determining whether a firm's shares are trading below their intrinsic value, particularly one he knows as deeply as the corporation he led for a long time. Abel is not Buffett, but he learned under the Oracle of Omaha's leadership, occupied high-level positions at Berkshire for a long time, and was handpicked to be Buffett's successor.

    However, we don't have to put our blind faith in Buffett and Abel (although in this case, that faith would hardly be blind). We can look at how the business is doing ourselves. Now, Berkshire Hathaway is a complex conglomerate with multiple moving parts. But Buffett himself gave us a framework to approximate the company's intrinsic value in a 2018 letter to shareholders.

    He argued that Berkshire Hathaway can be separated into five "groves," each of which can be valued separately. We can then get close to the business' total value by adding up the individual groves' values, making the appropriate adjustments (taxes, debt, etc.), and dividing that total by the number of shares outstanding to get the intrinsic value per share. By my calculation, Berkshire Hathaway is at the moment slightly undervalued, by about 8% to 10%, although the answer can change depending on the earnings multiple we apply to certain parts of the business.

    Sources indicate that but if my answer is roughly in agreement with that of Abel and Buffett -- who know infinitely more about Berkshire Hathaway than I do -- then I am fine with that. There is another aspect to consider. Berkshire Hathaway is arguably an outstanding hedge against current market uncertainty. Some are worried about a shaky geopolitical and economic environment.

    It has been revealed that others worry that AI stocks are overvalued and will drag broader equities into a bear market. Berkshire Hathaway has a vast and diversified business with multiple parts that will respond differently to whatever troubles lie ahead. The company also has some exposure to AI, though not too much, through its public equity portfolio, especially its stake in Alphabet (GOOG +0.14%) (GOOGL -0.29%). So, investors have a lot to gain by investing in the stock and holding onto it for a long time.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.
    • Sources indicate that the initial public offering (IPO) market has delivered two historic moments this year, and both involve the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.
    • But the celebration has faded quickly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adria Cimino – Nov 27, 2026 at 10:05AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

    Sources indicate that the initial public offering (IPO) market has delivered two historic moments this year, and both involve the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +3.63%) listed on the Nasdaq in June in what was then the largest IPO ever, and Anthropic (ANT +8.52%), the company behind the Claude AI models, topped that record with its own debut on Nov. 19.

    But the celebration has faded quickly. SpaceX shares trade well below their first-day closing price, and Anthropic closed below its $83 IPO price on Tuesday, just four trading days after its debut. Investors are grappling with a familiar worry: Are these companies spending too much?

    Industry observers note that both companies are growing at breathtaking speeds, and both are spending enormous sums to keep up. So which of these latest giants is the better buy today? Let's find out.

    Anthropic's growth is hard to ignore. Earlier this decade, Dario Amodei and a small group of fellow researchers left OpenAI and released this rival AI lab. And in 2023, Anthropic launched its first Claude AI model. Since then, it's released fresh versions and has seen revenue soar.

    Annual revenue climbed from $41 million in 2023 to $4.6 billion last year, and in the third quarter of this year, revenue topped $17 billion. Enterprise demand is driving this incredible momentum: More than 1,900 customers generated at least $1 million in revenue, and 250 customers were responsible for $10 million in revenue over the trailing 12 months.

    NASDAQ · As of 10:41 AM ET 11/27/26.

    According to recent reports, the company faces a number of risks, however, including the investment needed to develop its models over time. Anthropic must generate a certain level of revenue to pay for the enormous amounts of compute required. The company's revenue is mainly consumption-based and not subject to long-term contractual commitments, yet its infrastructure commitments extend over many years. The risk is that revenue won't keep up with these spending commitments.

    SpaceX's growth is just as impressive, and the manufacturer has made significant progress on profitability. In the third quarter, SpaceX reported net income of more than $4 billion, compared to a year-earlier loss of more than $1 billion.

    Recent findings suggest that the industrial and tech giant also has more than one engine, operating the Starlink connectivity business, the space business, and an AI segment. What's interesting here is that progress in reusable rockets may benefit all three businesses, as it ensures the tech giant's ability to launch critical materials into space. For example, reusable rockets may transport Starlink's satellites. This is more cost-effective and could help SpaceX advance more promptly toward its goals.

    NASDAQ · As of 10:43 AM ET 11/27/26.

    Industry observers note that then there's the potential Tesla merger. Musk has said he's considering a combination, and special committees at both companies are weighing a reported all-stock deal, according to press reports. Musk sees synergies in AI, chips, robotics, and orbital computing, though a deal would also add complexity.

    Sources indicate that spending is the concern here, too, as SpaceX's capital spending far exceeds its revenue. In the third quarter, capex surpassed $19 billion while revenue came it a $14 billion. Investors will want to see returns on this investment.

    Both stocks could reward patient investors, but each is spending heavily on AI infrastructure and faces the risk that returns may arrive later than expected. Still, SpaceX looks like the better buy today.

    Anthropic is essentially a single bet on enterprise AI demand, and much of its revenue depends on usage that customers can scale back. SpaceX, meanwhile, has Starlink generating real operating income, a launch business, and a fast-growing AI arm, so profits from one area can help fund growth in another. It was also profitable in the third quarter.

    That said, a Tesla deal isn't guaranteed, and both stocks may stay volatile as the post-IPO dust settles.

    10 stocks we like better than Celsius Holdings ›.

    Growth-oriented investors often debate between rapid expansion and established profitability. Choosing between Celsius (CELH +3.10%) and lululemon athletica (LULU +0.93%) requires weighing explosive functional beverage sales against steady athletic apparel dominance.

    It has been revealed that celsius focuses on the functional energy drink market, targeting health-conscious consumers with its proprietary formulas. lululemon athletica dominates the premium athletic apparel space with a loyal following. Both companies rely on strong brand identities to navigate the competitive consumer landscape, making them frequent candidates for long-term portfolios.

    Celsius develops and markets functional drinks that appeal to health-conscious consumers, a growing segment among beverage stocks. The company depends significantly on its partnership with Pepsi, which acts as the primary distributor for its products across the United States. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as Pepsi accounted for nearly 43.2% of total net revenue in its latest annual report.

    According to recent reports, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $3.2 billion. This figure reflects a revenue growth rate of approximately 49.1% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income for this time frame was close to $317 million, resulting in a net margin of approximately 10% during this phase of aggressive expansion.

    Sources indicate that as of its September 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is roughly 2.0x (1.97x), which measures a tech giant's ability to cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets. The debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.2x (0.22x), a metric that compares total debt against shareholder equity to evaluate financial leverage. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $269.0 million, which is the cash remaining after paying for operating costs and equipment.

    It has been revealed that lululemon athletica operates an omni-channel retail model that combines more than 800 company-operated stores with an expansive digital presence. The brand serves a global audience in 30 markets, offering technical athletic apparel and footwear designed for performance. By leveraging wholesale partnerships with fitness studios and international license arrangements, the company maintains a premium presence in the global apparel market.

    In the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached approximately $11.1 billion. This represents a revenue growth rate of nearly 1.7% over the previous twelve months. Net income during this timeframe was roughly $1.4 billion, yielding a net margin of close to 12.8% as the organization focuses on balancing scale with profitability.

    Industry observers note that as of its February 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is roughly 2.3x. The debt-to-equity ratio stands at approximately 0.4x, indicating the level of total debt used to finance tech giant assets relative to shareholder equity. In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $921.7 million, providing the company with substantial capital to reinvest in its global operations.

    Celsius faces significant concentration risks because a single distributor, Pepsi, accounts for a massive portion of its revenue and receivables. The manufacturer must also defend its market share against large-scale competitors such as Monster Beverage (MNST -0.06%) and The Coca-Cola Company (KO -0.23%). Furthermore, the brand is vulnerable to potential regulatory actions regarding its health claims and must navigate supply chain complexities for materials like aluminum.

    Recent findings suggest that lululemon athletica is currently managing uncertainty following a leadership transition and potential brand reputation risks in a crowded apparel market. The company faces intense competition from established global firms and must protect its premium positioning amid shifting consumer discretionary spending habits. Additionally, it is managing class action litigation related to demand projections while handling complex supply chain dependencies in the Asia-Pacific region.

    Sources indicate that based on Forward P/E and P/S multiples, lululemon athletica appears to be the more conservatively valued option for investors.     I'd go with Celsius. It has built a multi-brand energy drink company with PepsiCo's delivery network behind it, and it is profitable and just beginning to expand overseas. An exciting part of this business right now is Alani Nu, a real growth engine. Celsius bought the brand last year and now its top seller, with retail sales up about 50% year over year even without its record seasonal flavor, a hit that will be tough to repeat. Celsius does have things to work through, though. Its namesake brand is shrinking, higher aluminum and fuel costs are squeezing margins, and an investor lawsuit and a Texas investigation into how its drinks are marketed add uncertainty. Still, Alani Nu's growth lifted total sales 17%.

    It has been revealed that lululemon still has a premium brand, plenty of cash and a new CEO focused on a turnaround. But its momentum has stalled, with sales shrinking. North American shoppers are buying less at existing stores, and the full-year outlook was trimmed in September. Its stock is cheaper than Celsius's relative to expected earnings, but it comes with a business that has yet to turn the corner.

    Celsius, meanwhile, is growing where lululemon is struggling. For long-term investors who can handle some bumps and a higher price, a profitable, growing beverage company makes Celsius the better buy for 2027.

    10 stocks we like better than ServiceNow ›.

    As businesses race to integrate artificial intelligence, choosing between enterprise workflow automation and semiconductor design tools involves weighing two different growth engines. Should you favor ServiceNow (NOW +0.43%) or Synopsys (SNPS +3.19%)?

    ServiceNow provides a cloud platform that streamlines corporate operations, while Synopsys builds the software essential for designing the next generation of chips. Both companies benefit from the digital transformation trend, but their business models target different layers of the technology stack, making them intriguing options for investors seeking growth.

    ServiceNow provides an enterprise software platform that connects data and workflows to automate functions like HR and customer service. The firm serves roughly 8,700 enterprise customers across various industries, utilizing its platform to streamline complex corporate processes. Its growth strategy involves deep integration with artificial intelligence and strategic technology alliances with partners like Microsoft (MSFT +0.46%), NVIDIA (NVDA -0.89%), and OpenAI.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $15.4 billion, growing roughly 21.8%. Net income for the period was close to $1.4 billion. These results reflect a consistent expansion in the adoption of cloud-based automation tools as organizations prioritize digital efficiency.

    According to recent reports, as of its September 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 0.7x (0.72x), which indicates the ability to pay short-term obligations using current assets. The debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.6x (0.64x), measuring total debt against shareholder equity. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $4.8 billion ($4,750 million), representing cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.6% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    Synopsys offers engineering solutions that span from silicon design to system analysis, supporting industries like aerospace, automotive, and healthcare. The firm is a key player among semiconductor stocks by providing essential tools for creating advanced chips and autonomous machines. Its growth is bolstered by its merger with Ansys and a partnership with Microsoft to deliver cloud-based design solutions.

    It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, revenue reached approximately $9.4 billion, which represents growth of roughly 46.3%. Net income during this period was nearly $1.1 billion. This significant increase in revenue highlights the expanding demand for engineering solutions as more industries transition toward connected technology and advanced silicon design.

    As of its July 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is close to 1.3x (1.34x), measuring the ability to cover short-term liabilities with current assets. The debt-to-equity ratio, which measures financial leverage by dividing total debt by shareholder equity, is approximately 0.3x (0.35x). In the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, free cash flow was roughly $2.7 billion ($2,748 million). Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 32.3% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    Recent findings suggest that serviceNow faces risks related to cybersecurity and data privacy, including potential vulnerabilities within AI-integrated code or third-party platforms. The company also navigates challenges in integrating artificial intelligence technology, specifically regarding legal and ethical risks that may impact regulatory compliance. Additionally, the increasing complexity of large enterprise deals often results in longer sales cycles and pricing pressure. There is also volatility in the public sector business, where government procurement processes and potential bid protests can impact results.

    Synopsys carries significant indebtedness following its merger with Ansys, which limits its financial flexibility and requires substantial cash flow for debt service. The firm is also exposed to geopolitical and trade regulation risks, particularly involving U.S. and Chinese trade policies that impact the semiconductor supply chain. Furthermore, Synopsys faces securities litigation and class action lawsuits related to its Design IP segment. Competition remains intense in the electronic design automation market from rivals like Cadence Design Systems (CDNS +0.97%), and the company must also manage the integration risks associated with its large-scale merger.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    Recent findings suggest that I'd go with ServiceNow. Big companies lean on its software every day, from IT help desks to HR requests, and now it is weaving AI into the mix. Here's the best part: With a 98% renewal rate, almost every customer sticks around.

    AI is already adding up. Management expects its AI products to reach $1.7 billion in yearly contracts by year-end, and overall sales are still growing at a fast clip, though the revenue it has already lined up for the next year is expected to grow a bit more slowly.

    In a recent development, synopsys is well placed, too. It sells the software engineers use to design computer chips, and AI is making those chips harder to design. But much of its recent growth came from buying Ansys, which loaded it with debt, and export limits on China weigh on parts of its business.

    Sources indicate that serviceNow, meanwhile, has fewer moving parts. For long-term investors, software that customers almost never leave, with AI adding a upcoming growth leg, makes ServiceNow the better buy for 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 27, 2026 at 10:38AM EST.
    • Sources indicate that realty Income (O +0.11%) is the largest net-lease real estate investment trust (REIT).
    • Industry observers note that realty Income is a net lease REIT, which means its tenants pay for most property-level operating costs.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 27, 2026 at 10:38AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Realty Income ›.

    Sources indicate that realty Income (O +0.11%) is the largest net-lease real estate investment trust (REIT). It offers an ultra-high 5.5% yield, which is well above the market's 1% and the average REIT's 3.6%. And if you invested $100,000 in Realty Income today, you would be netting yourself a monthly dividend check of roughly $458. Here's the math behind that number and why retired investors should find it so appealing.

    Industry observers note that realty Income is a net lease REIT, which means its tenants pay for most property-level operating costs. That reduces the REIT's expenses and mitigates the risks that come with operating a property. In the real estate world, using net leases is a fairly low-risk business model, assuming you have a large enough portfolio. Generally, net lease properties are single-tenant assets, so each individual property has material risk if the tenant leaves. Realty Income owns over 15,500 properties, which materially reduces tenant risk.

    That's not the only way the organization mitigates risk, however. For example, it focuses on retail properties (about 77% of rents), which are generally the easiest net lease assets to buy, sell, and release as needed. It adds a little diversification through industrial properties and more unique assets, such as casinos and data centers. In addition, the portfolio is spread across North America and Europe, providing yet another layer of diversification. More recently, the company has begun offering debt financing, entering into partnerships, and providing asset management services.

    In a recent development, meanwhile, the company has long focused on operating with a strong financial core. To that point, it has an investment-grade-rated balance sheet and is a member of the S&P 500 index (^GSPC +1.23%). Put all of this together, and Realty Income tends to have advantaged access to capital markets, which gives it a leg up on its REIT competitors. All of this goes a long way in explaining the company's impressive 32-year dividend streak.

    Industry observers note that what's even more interesting for retired dividend investors, however, is the firm's trademarked nickname: The Monthly Dividend Company. That not only speaks to Realty Income's commitment to its dividend but also highlights the monthly pay schedule. Monthly dividends make it easier to budget than quarterly dividends, since you get a new influx of cash at more frequent intervals. Even better, Realty Income has a long history of making quarterly dividend increases, so you are getting a regular check and regular "pay raises.".

    NYSE · As of 10:44 AM ET 11/27/26.

    Recent findings suggest that to put some numbers on all of this, a $100,000 investment in Realty Income at the time of this writing would buy roughly 1,674 shares. Given the current dividend rate of $0.274 per share per month, that would translate into a monthly check of roughly $458. Over a full quarter, you'd collect three dividend payments, bringing the total to $1,376. Over a full year, which would mean collecting 12 monthly dividends, you'd come away with just over $5,500.

    Recent findings suggest that that's a very solid foundation for a diversified dividend portfolio. It could give you the leeway to buy lower-yielding stocks with rapidly growing dividends. Or even give you the confidence to lean into high-yielding stocks with riskier business profiles, such as an out-of-favor consumer staples or healthcare company. The key is that you aren't just getting income; you are getting options. And the history of regular, though modest, quarterly dividend increases makes the story all the more compelling.

    Sources indicate that A $100,000 investment may be massive or small, depending on your financial situation. You can scale the math up or down to fit your needs, but the basic story remains the same. Realty Income is a reliable, monthly-paying dividend stock with an attractive yield. And it is built from the ground up to keep paying you no matter what the market throws at it. Dividend investors tend to be a pretty boring group; however, Realty Income's dividend opens up options that even the most conservative investor should find exciting.

    Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (520 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
    • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
    • Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting substantial moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the firm that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, mentioned in a text ahead of the organization's after-market report on Tuesday.

    It has been revealed that since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is currently 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    In a recent development, one catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    Recent findings suggest that with bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (734 w)

    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Here’s Why I’d Still Buy Nvidia Over AMD With or Without Jensen Huang at CEO.

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (734 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia (NVDA -0.89%) and AMD (AMD +2.43%) are rivals.
    • However, Nvidia's investment thesis recently hit a bump in the road due to issues involving co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang.
    • But Huang isn’t out of the woods yet, as he must testify before Congress about recent events.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keithen Drury – Nov 27, 2026 at 10:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Nvidia (NVDA -0.89%) and AMD (AMD +2.43%) are rivals. These companies compete in multiple industries, but none as massive as data centers right now. Both AMD and Nvidia have strong product offerings. Still, Nvidia took an early lead due to having better software, and that was all it took for Nvidia's product lineup to become the go-to in the data center industry.

    However, Nvidia's investment thesis recently hit a bump in the road due to issues involving co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang. Huang resigned due to misconduct issues, but was reinstated by the board a few days later.

    But Huang isn’t out of the woods yet, as he must testify before Congress about recent events. This could cause a distraction, and Nvidia's issues undoubtedly give AMD an advantage right now/.

    But I still don't think it's even close to enough to consider investing in AMD over Nvidia.

    Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

    According to recent reports, the best way to compare these two stocks is to look at how their respective data center businesses are doing. This offers a more direct comparison and reveals to investors how each is doing in the most crucial sector.

    In a recent development, AMD and Nvidia's third quarters don't end at the same time. AMD operates on a calendar-year fiscal schedule, with its Q3 ending on Sept. 30. Nvidia's is shifted 13 months forward, with its fiscal 2027 Q3 ending on Oct. 25, so a perfect comparison isn't possible. Still, it's the best investors have.

    It has been revealed that AMD's data center revenue grew in Q3 at a 97% pace to $8.5 billion. Those are strong results, but they fall well short of Nvidia's. During its fiscal 2027 third quarter, Nvidia's data center revenue totaled $107.6 billion, up 110% compared to a year ago. So, not only is Nvidia far larger, but it's also growing appreciably faster. Those two factors are rarely combined, which is what makes Nvidia so dominant.

    However, all those results were obtained before the concerns surrounding Huang and China export concerns came to light. While some may think this will affect Nvidia's growth and sales, I'm not sure it will. The reality is that the AI hyperscalers cannot get their hands on as much computing power as they want right now. So, regardless of who is selling the computing unit to them, they want it. As a result, AMD's and Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) are practically selling themselves. This is a great place to be, and Nvidia will likely be able to ride out the status quo it established until the situation gets a bit more under control.

    Sources indicate that right now, Nvidia is still winning and will likely do so for some time. What will happen a couple of years down the road is unknown, but with Huang keeping his role, the future is bright for Nvidia. However, that's not the only reason Nvidia is a buy over AMD.

    After Nvidia's heavy sell-off, the stock is very cheap right now. On the flip side, AMD's stock is a bit pricey after an impressive run in 2026.

    NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

    Industry observers note that with Nvidia trading at an incredibly cheap 9.3 times next year's earnings estimates, it's about two and a half times cheaper than AMD at around 23.5 times next year's earnings estimates. That's a gigantic mismatch, and it stems from skepticism about the AI build-out.

    However, CFO Colette Kress eliminated that thought during Nvidia's most recent conference call when she increased the company’s guidance for revenue growth in fiscal 2028 from 70% to 75%.

    In a recent development, that's monster growth that the market isn't pricing in, and the stock is cheap as a result. So, regardless of who's leading the tech giant, I think Nvidia is a far better investment than AMD is right now.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the tech giant "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    In a recent development, the report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the organization kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also noted that new export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    In a recent development, the allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson remarked in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the firm's recent earnings call that China is an "important" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    The Philadelphia 76ers could be short-staffed when they take on the Indiana Pacers in NBA Cup play on Friday night.

    Shooting guard Jaylen Brown has already been ruled out with a hamstring injury. Center Joel Embiid is listed as questionable due to a lingering illness that has sidelined him for Philadelphia's last two games.

    Sources indicate that brown picked up the hamstring glitch in Wednesday's NBA Cup win over the Miami Heat. He left the game late in the first half and did not return.     Toward the end of the first half, the Philadelphia guard reached toward his left hamstring and shook his head before checking himself out of the game.

    Embiid is dealing with an illness, though not much has been released about what symptoms he may be dealing with. Regardless, he has missed two consecutive games. The center was listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Heat, but was downgraded before the game.

    With no Embiid and no Brown for a half, LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey took over and led the 76ers to a win over the Heat on Wednesday. James logged his first triple-double as a 76er with 25 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists. Maxey added 30 points, 4 rebounds and 6 assists.

    The win moved Philadelphia to 15-4. Friday's game against Indiana is the front end of a back-to-back, and a win would help the 76ers clinch their NBA Cup group.

    #222745. Tech Report: Taking on Starlink: Europe’s largest satellite factory opens in push to rival Musk

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (437 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Taking on Starlink: Europe’s largest satellite factory opens in push to rival Musk

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (437 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The largest satellite factory in Europe was inaugurated in Belgium this week, boosting the continent's efforts to challenge Elon Musk's Starlink and reduce reliance on U.S.
    • Privately held Belgian satellite manufacturer Aerospacelab secured a 2.4-billion-euro ($2.6 billion) contract in September to manufacture 264 of the 348 satellites planned for IRIS², the European Union's answer to SpaceX's Starlink business.
    • Aerospacelab noted this will "form the backbone of Europe's sovereign, secure, and resilient connectivity infrastructure by 2030." It will be named Ectro from Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The largest satellite factory in Europe was inaugurated in Belgium this week, boosting the continent's efforts to challenge Elon Musk's Starlink and reduce reliance on U.S. space infrastructure.

    Privately held Belgian satellite manufacturer Aerospacelab secured a 2.4-billion-euro ($2.6 billion) contract in September to manufacture 264 of the 348 satellites planned for IRIS², the European Union's answer to SpaceX's Starlink business.

    Aerospacelab noted this will "form the backbone of Europe's sovereign, secure, and resilient connectivity infrastructure by 2030." It will be named Ectro from Nov. 30.

    Its latest oval-shaped, 20,000-square-meter facility in southern Belgium, inaugurated by Belgian King Philippe, will be able to produce up to 500 satellites annually, which would make it the world's third-largest satellite production site, according to the Belgian royal palace.

    Employees are expected to move into the megafactory in January, and production is slated to begin by the end of 2028, according to AFP.

    Satellite connectivity has become increasingly important to everyday life as well as national security.

    It provides internet access to remote locations and defense equipment like warships and fighter jets, and lets governments and militaries communicate securely where Earth-based networks are unavailable or disrupted.

    It has been revealed that the importance of such capabilities has become particularly apparent in Ukraine, as the country's military relies heavily on Starlink connectivity to fight Russian forces. Recent restrictions to the service over Russian-occupied territory reported by Ukrainian officials further underscored the way geopolitical conflict may depend on commercial businesses.

    But Europe still has a long way to go in challenging Starlink's dominance.

    SpaceX states it has more than 11,000 Starlink satellites in low Earth orbit, making it by far the largest satellite constellation in the world, and prepares up to 100,000 satellites.

    Among the challengers is Amazon, whose satellite business, Amazon Leo, has deployed over 400 satellites and plans an initial in-orbit constellation of more than 3,200.

    Meanwhile, French Eutelsat operates more than 600 satellites in low Earth orbit through its OneWeb constellation. The organization is also part of the SpaceRISE consortium alongside SES and Hispasat, tasked with developing and operating IRIS².

    The European Commission has called IRIS² a "strategic asset to achieve space sovereignty in the face of commercial satellite constellations, such as Starlink." The aim is for first debuts to take place by the end of 2029, with initial services expected soon after.

    In August, the Commission and SpaceRISE consortium announced they were expanding the main constellation from 282 to 348 satellites, increasing its secure communications capacity for EU governments by 60%.

    Defense and security applications were the main drivers of the expanded scope, the Commission noted.

    #222742. Latest Update: Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (757 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a massive win for the organization and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    It has been revealed that some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Industry observers note that adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and noted it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the significant indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    In a recent development, "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he stated.

    According to recent reports, part of the challenge, Niles said, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    According to recent reports, "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," noted JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he mentioned, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan stated. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the firm in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    According to recent reports, "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he remarked. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    It has been revealed that one bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.
